response.text:
The notes say the invoice amount (INV_AMT) differs from the 2000 credit amount, and that this was the only such mismatch. They do not say which amount is correct, and I can't query the database to check. A typo on the credit side is the most likely explanation, so I treat the 14,689.28 debit as the true figure. The debit also matches the stated INV_AMT. A payment, if any, would equal the invoice amount, which also points to 14,689.28.

The fix is a one-sided credit of 45.00 to 2000. The original credit of 14,644.28 plus my 45.00 gives 14,689.28, which balances the 14,689.28 debit. I post it in open period 12, the same period as the original journal. No invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate invoice finding.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 1597 debits 5400 for 14,689.28 but credits AP 2000 for only 14,644.28 (short by 45.00). The debit matches the invoice amount (INV_AMT), so the AP credit is the mistyped side. A one-sided credit of 45.00 to 2000 in open period 12 brings AP to 14,689.28 and balances the journal group. No invoice status is changed.
